items.headline: Savannah Resources signs benefit‑sharing deals for Portugal’s largest spodumene lithium deposit
items.title: Savannah Resources signs agreements with local communities for Barroso lithium project
items.scifi_hook: A European lithium mine locks in community pacts to unlock a strategic battery metal source.
items.eli5: The company agreed to share benefits with local villages near a big lithium rock in Portugal.
items.why: It secures social license for a key European battery‑material project.
items.text: Savannah Resources (LON: SAV) said on Wednesday it has signed three benefit sharing agreements with local communities that hold and manage communal lands (baldios) near the Barroso lithium project in Portugal. Barroso has been deemed a ‘Strategic Project’ under the European Critical Raw Materials Act and Europe’s largest spodumene lithium deposit. In 2025, Savannah lifted the reserve estimate by 40%. The London-listed company now pegs reserves at more than 39 million tonnes, up from a previous estimate of 28 million tonnes. Despite its strategic significance, the project has been met with opposition from local communities and environmental groups. The Barroso region, recognized as a World Heritage agricultural site since 2018, has raised concerns over potential impacts on land use, water and biodiversity. Benefit sharing agreements have now been signed with the Baldio of the villages of Alijó, Canedo and Penalonga, another with the Baldio of the Couto de Dornelas, and a third with the regional Secretariat of the Baldios of Trás-os-Montes and Alto Douro. A land access and benefit sharing agreement with the Baldio of the villages of Alijó, Canedo and Penalonga include Blocks A and C of the Aldeia mining concession, the company said. items.headline: Researchers achieve single‑domain state in altermagnetic material
items.title: Uniaxial strain reveals new way to tune electron flow in altermagnet material
items.scifi_hook: Scientists flip a new kind of magnet into a uniform state, opening a path to cooler, faster memory.
items.eli5: They aligned a novel magnetic material so its tiny magnets all point the same way, letting them study it.
items.why: It could lead to low‑heat, high‑density computing components.
items.text: Altermagnetism is a new, third type of magnetism of great interest for spin-transport applications like computer memory. If properly harnessed, it could combine the benefits of the two existing types of magnetism, ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, ultimately reducing or eliminating heat during information transfer and increasing the ability to miniaturize next-generation technologies. Rice University's Pengcheng Dai recently published a paper in Physical Review X describing the first successful efforts to put a proposed altermagnetic material into a single magnetic-domain state, allowing the research team to characterize the material's intrinsic magnetic structure.

items.headline: Super El Niño could hit Africa by 2026, raising extreme‑weather risks
items.title: Understanding the emerging super El-nino threat in Africa
items.scifi_hook: Scientists warn a rare, powerful El Niño may slam East Africa with record heat and drought.
items.eli5: A very strong warming of Pacific ocean waters could cause unusually harsh weather in Africa through 2026‑27.
items.why: Severe climate swings threaten food security and livelihoods for millions.
items.text: Africa is bracing for the possible impacts of a powerful El Nino event that could develop through 2026 and continue into 2027, raising concerns over extreme weather, food security and livelihoods across the continent. El Nino occurs when sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become unusually warm. The warming can alter atmospheric circulation and disrupt weather patterns thousands of kilometres away. "There have been observations by the US meteorological agencies around the Pacific Ocean. Whenever the ocean warms up, there is a lot of rearrangement in terms of the climate and how it affects us here in East Africa. What has been observed currently is that there is a four-to-five chance that it's going to be a super El Nino," according to Dr James Mumina, a research scientist at the University of Sussex. What could it mean for Africa? The effects of El Nino vary across the continent, depending on the region, season and interaction with other climate systems.
